articleHeadline: The first PCR test rules out Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in the patient admitted to Virgen del Rocío.
articleSummary: PCR testing at Hospital Virgen del Rocío in Seville has ruled out Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever in a patient with high suspicion of the disease. The patient remains isolated in the High-Level Isolation and Treatment Unit (UATAN) while investigations seek the illness’ origin; definitive results are expected by late Wednesday after samples were sent to the National Center for Microbiology of the Carlos III Health Institute. A previously reported potential case in Seville involved a traveler from Zambia via Doha; the Italian-born resident in Spain was visiting family when symptoms—fever, dizziness and gastrointestinal bleeding—appeared. The initial PCR panel excluded a broad range of pathogens, including chikungunya, dengue, West Nile virus, Ebola, Lassa, Marburg, and Zika, as well as Bacillus anthracis, Francisella tularensis, Leptospira, Salmonella Typhi/Paratyphi, Yersinia pestis, and Plasmodium species. Transfer between hospitals followed strict isolation, with a fully protected ambulance and police coordination to maintain containment.

articleHeadline: In Russia, imported cases of West Nile fever from three countries were detected.
articleSummary: West Nile fever cases in Russia since the season's start are sporadic, mainly on endemic territories, with several imported from Thailand, Mali, and the Central African Republic. Rosptrebnadzor reports no West Nile fever–related deaths in 2026. The virus is described as spreading across Russia at about 92 km per year. An August 8 outbreak was detected in Ukraine's Sumy region, while in Russia's Volgograd region the first case was confirmed on July 13 in a resident of the regional capital. Birds and rodents are the primary natural reservoirs. The report notes imported cases from non-endemic countries and local transmissions within Russia, illustrating a mix of imported and autochthonous activity during the current epidemic season.
